text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000213 bills 99215 well above expectation even after risk adjustment, but documentation is too thin to say whether this reflects upcoding or a genuinely complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel does skew complex, and most 99215s fall on patients with many chronic conditions, so complexity explains part of the pattern. It does not explain all of it: the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running well above the all-provider share in every stratum, including patients with zero or one condition, such as the acute-URI visits C0105031 and C0105209. The records review cannot settle the question because only a handful of 99215 charts came back. Two were below the billed level (C0105545, C0106017) and three supported high MDM (e.g., C0104983), a split the rule check treats as too small to call, and no data-reviewed notes lacked a supporting lab or test line. A reviewer should first request more 99215 charts, prioritizing the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, to see whether the above-peer coding within each complexity stratum is backed by documented high MDM or time."}
